content: Advanced wound therapies, as recommended by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), include various oxygen-based treatments. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy involves exposing the patient to 100% oxygen at pressures higher than atmospheric levels, which enhances oxygen delivery to hypoxic tissues, promoting angiogenesis, collagen synthesis, and overall wound healing. Topical oxygen therapy delivers oxygen directly to the wound site, improving local oxygenation and supporting cellular repair processes. Additionally, oxygen-releasing sprays provide a controlled release of oxygen to the wound environment, which can aid in reducing bacterial load, minimizing infection risk, and accelerating tissue regeneration.
